issues.failure_explanation: Both key steps are non sequiturs. (i) Vanishing of the fully truncated function on Q only forces the mother (and hence the members of R, whose two-scale coefficients are positive and whose supports lie in the mother's support) to vanish on Q\Ω_{ℓ̃+1}; it does not imply supp ⊆ Ω_{ℓ̃}: a level-ℓ̃ component of the mother can have support leaving Ω_{ℓ̃} outside Q, with its on-Q contribution removed by truncations at finer levels, so the stated implication is unestablished. (ii) The inclusion R' ⊆ G does not follow from β^{j'} being a k-derivation of the mother: the level-ℓ̃ representation of the single derivation is not obtained from the level-ℓ̃ representation of the mother; proving the inclusion requires a two-scale (refinement–derivation commutation) analysis that is not given.

failure_location.quote: We must have \(\mathcal{R}^{\boldvec{j}'}_{\meshel, \tilde{\level}} \subseteq \mathcal{G}^{\boldvec{j}'}_{\meshel, \tilde{\level}}\), because \(\bsp^{\boldvec{j}'}_{\boldvec{i}', \level}\) is just one of the \(k\)-derivations of \(\bsp^{\boldvec{j}}_{\boldvec{i}, \level}\).

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove the Ω_{ℓ̃}-containment by an induction over truncation levels (showing surviving components' on-Q contributions are removed at finer levels) and prove R' ⊆ G via non-negativity of two-scale coefficients and index counting, as in standard spline refinement theory.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof asserts (a) that for each level-ℓ 0-form one can find 0-forms at every coarser level whose supports form a nested chain down to level 0, and (b) implicitly, that on the violating element Q̃ there is an active 0-form of Q̃'s own level (needed to obtain two active 0-forms whose levels differ by ≥ m on a common element). Neither follows from the paper's only standing hypothesis, mere nestedness of the level spaces: e.g. under degree elevation a finer B-spline's support (ξ_i, ξ_{i+p'+1}) with p' > p is contained in no coarser support (ξ_j, ξ_{j+p+1}), so the asserted chain need not exist. Both facts hold for h-refinement (via non-negative two-scale coefficients and Assumption 1), but the refinement class is never restricted and the auxiliary arguments are missing.

issues.failure_explanation: Because S^0 vanishes on ∂[0,1]^2, every function in the discrete 1-form space S^{(1,0)}×S^{(0,1)} (and in every hierarchical analogue) has vanishing tangential trace on ∂Ω (the y-factor of any element of S^{(1,0)} lies in S^0 and vanishes at y∈{0,1}, etc.). Hence ∫_Ω curl v = 0 for every discrete v, while the top space S^{(1,1)} = S^1⊗S^1, which carries no boundary conditions, contains functions of nonzero integral (the constant 1 for L=0; any active positive top-form B-spline for L≥1). Therefore curl(S^1) ⊊ S^2 always: the complex of eq:hierarchical-complex has at least one-dimensional cohomology at the top space and is never exact. thm:added-1 already fails for L=0 with Ω_1 = ∅, where its hypothesis holds vacuously; the quoted source ([Shepherd2024, Thm 4.24]) is valid for the standard complex without boundary conditions, and as restated for these spaces the conclusion is false. The same convention contradicts the numerical section: u = (x(1−x),0) is not in T^1_L (its first component does not vanish at y∈{0,1}, whereas every element of T^{(1,0)}_L does), so the reported error ≈ 4.9·10^{-16} is impossible under the stated definitions; and the Maxwell kernel count 'dim(T^0_L) minus boundary DoFs' presupposes boundary DoFs in T^0_L, although under the stated definition ∇ is injective on T^0_L (its elements vanish on ∂Ω) and the kernel would have dimension dim(T^0_L). The discrete cohomology (0,0,1) also does not match the continuous complex's (1,0,0), contradicting the Section 3 cohomological-equivalence claim.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either (i) replace the p-fold boundary-knot convention by standard open knot vectors (p+1 repetitions, no vanishing condition on S^0), matching the quoted theorem's setting and the numerical implementation, adjusting the dimension formulas and boundary-DoF discussion accordingly; or (ii) keep the boundary conditions, restrict the top space to zero-mean functions, and restate all exactness claims for the resulting relative complex.
issues.overall_effect: The paper's central guarantee — that the constructed and algorithmically repaired hierarchical complex is exact — fails for every instance of the stated construction; the Section 3 cohomology claim, lem:added-1, and the internal consistency of the entire numerical validation are compromised.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Moreover, we say that \(\xbsp_{\boldvec{i}} \in \Bll\) is resolved in direction \(k\) if \(		\sideconfig_{\boldvec{i}, k} \subseteq \Bll.\)

issues.failure_explanation: Definition def:resolved only says that the two side-neighbours of β_i are refined; it says nothing about their distance to β_j. The asserted neighbour exists only when i_k ≠ j_k; if i_k = j_k, both side-neighbours satisfy |t_k − j_k| = 1 > 0 = |i_k − j_k|, so the proof's first step is false as written. The lemma survives only because a problematic pair with i_k = j_k cannot exist (if the supports coincide in direction k, all intermediate functions of the straight chain between i and j have supports covered by supp β_i ∪ supp β_j ⊆ Ω_{ℓ+1}, so a shortest chain exists and the pair is not problematic) — a nontrivial fact the paper neither states nor proves. The proof also does not verify that the selected β_t is the neighbour lying toward β_j, which is needed for the length computation.

failure_location.quote: Since \(\xbsp_{\boldvec{i}}\) is resolved in direction \(k\), by definition there exists \(\xbsp_{\boldvec{t}}\in \sideconfig_{\boldvec{i}, k}\) such that \(\abs{t_k - j_k} < \abs{i_k - j_k}\).

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the missing case analysis: first show that problematic pairs have different indices in both directions (via the support-covering argument), then choose the side-neighbour lying toward β_j.

issues.failure_explanation: lem:problematic-sides transfers problematic-ness from a chain member to a side-neighbour closer to β_l. Nothing in the argument shows that this walk stays inside the L-chain or stops at an endpoint or the corner: interior arm members are resolved only along the arm, so the walk proceeds along an arm toward β_i, β_j or β_c; but if such an endpoint is resolved in the arm direction (its outward neighbour refined — not excluded by any hypothesis), the walk steps off the chain, and if the resulting function is unresolved the recursion halts at a function outside {β_i, β_j, β_c}, leaving the stated conclusion unestablished. No termination measure for the recursion is given either.

issues.failure_explanation: Membership in the interaction box only bounds the index distance of β_l and β_t by 2(p+1) in Chebyshev norm, whereas two level-ℓ 0-form B-splines have intersecting (closed) supports only if their indices differ by at most p+1 in each direction. In the 'wide' direction of □_{i,j} (width up to 2(p+1)−|e|), two chain members sharing their index in the other direction can be more than p+1 apart; then their closed supports are disjoint, so the claimed non-empty intersection fails, and the covering supp(β_r) ⊆ supp(β_l) ∪ supp(β_t) fails for intermediate β_r because a gap opens between the two supports. The kink-removal/straightening argument on which the proof rests is therefore not established.

failure_location.quote: since \(\xbsp_{\boldvec{l}}\) and \(\xbsp_{\boldvec{t}}\) are both in \(\interbox{\boldvec{i}}{\boldvec{j}}\), their supports have a non-empty intersection, which implies that \(\supp(\xbsp_{\boldvec{r}}) \subseteq \overline{\supp(\xbsp_{\boldvec{l}})} \cup \overline{\supp(\xbsp_{\boldvec{t}})} \subseteq \Omega_{\level+1} \)

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either prove the covering using the full set of chain members and the closure of \Bll under support covering (a member whose support is covered by a union of refined supports is itself refined), or prove that kinks with index distance exceeding p+1 in the wide direction cannot occur for chains contained in □_{i,j}.

issues.failure_explanation: (i) The variable unchecked_funcs is never initialised in alg:exact-mesh (it is local to alg:initiate-unchecked), so the set from which new pairs are generated is undefined. (ii) After an L-chain is added, the only pairs re-examined are pairs among the accumulated corner functions; but by lem:problematic-chain — the very result invoked to justify the procedure — a new problematic pair after the addition has the form (β_l, β_i), (β_l, β_j) or (β_l, β_c), where β_l is an arbitrary function of \Bll sharing a minimal (ℓ+1)-intersection with a chain member; in particular β_l need not itself be a corner, so pairs (β_l, corner) with β_l outside the accumulated set are never checked and the while-loop can terminate with problematic pairs undetected. (iii) No termination argument is given (beyond finiteness of \Bll), and no argument connects the procedure to the chain condition of thm:added-1; lem:added-1's 'proof' merely cites three lemmas without relating them to the algorithm's coverage or output.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Initialise and maintain the set of functions requiring re-checking (all functions of \Bll whose support meets the newly marked region, together with the new chain members), derive the new-pair generation from lem:problematic-chain, and supply an actual proof of lem:added-1 (termination via strict growth of the marked set, correctness via the chain condition of thm:added-1).
issues.overall_effect: The algorithm's stated guarantee — returning a basis 'with no problematic intersections' and hence (via thm:added-1) an exact complex — is not established, and as specified the procedure can miss problematic pairs.
